div.div: Asynchronous relative to the periodic interrupt source. For instance a pin interrupt from an external system or another core independent event.

div.div: Simple use-case where the device remain in the shutdown state with the WDT enabled until a counter has reached a value, N, and it's time to restart the application.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 388px; height: 1px; padding-top: 426px; margin-left: 752px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0px; text-align: left;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: normal;

div.div:
In this scenario, the device waits for an external event before restarting the application. When it occurs, the API is used to request a reset. In the meantime, the periodic interrupt ensures the WDT is cleared before it times out.
Due to it being asynchronous, there is a risk of a race condition where the interrupt occurs after the exit request is evaluated, in which the device re-enters sleep and the exit request is only re-evaluated once the next periodic interrupt occurs. If the worst case delay is not acceptable, it is possible to issue software reset directly in the ISR or have an external system trigger an external reset through the reset pin.

switch.text: In this scenario, the device waits for an external event before r...

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 398px; height: 1px; padding-top: 426px; margin-left: 1202px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0px; text-align: left;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: normal;

div.div:
In this scenario, the WDT is disabled and does not need to be cleared periodically. The device can sleep until an external event occurs and exit can be requested. Since the device is already in a Safe State, the WDT can be safely disabled. This will reduce power consumption further.
However, should there be any stuck code, there is a risk that the device will not automatically reset, but the SWDT may time out and signal the error controller. Should the device be stuck in sleep, i.e., the configured wake-up source does not wake the device correctly, there is a risk of not exiting properly without the WDT enabled. It is thus recommended to apply an external reset to ensure application reliability.

div.div: If required, any additional interrupt sources may wake the device and go back to sleep. In this case, the SWDT will eventually time out, so it can be cleared each time you wake up.
